content.text:
I submitted **index 35** (Cr 0.15, Fe 0.52, V 0.33). It had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I could measure: **2.89 µA**. I can't tell whether it's the best composition in the 201-sample library, because three measurements cover very little of it.

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 147 | 0.23 / 0.28 / 0.50 | 0.45 µA |
| **35** | **0.15 / 0.52 / 0.33** | **2.89 µA** |
| 45 | 0.16 / 0.59 / 0.25 | 1.79 µA |

- **How I chose the samples:** For the first, I picked a V-rich composition close to FeVO₄, a known photoanode material, with some Cr added. The model's suggestion after that one measurement was not useful, since its uncertainty was larger than its predictions. So I tried the Fe-rich region instead, which gave about 6× more photocurrent. My last measurement moved further toward Fe (index 45), and the merit dropped. That suggests a peak somewhere around Fe ~0.5, V ~0.3.
- **Not checked:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the crystal structures behind these results are unknown. The phase list from the database was too long to return, and I didn't read the saved copy. The high-V corner (V ≈ 0.7–0.8), where many of the library samples sit, and the Cr-rich compositions were never measured.
